cases.prompt:
Loyalty extract columns: customer_id, full_name, email, mobile, dob, street_address, last_order_total.
Our policy (pii_type,handling): email,tokenize · phone,mask · dob,drop · name,mask.
Which columns are PII and what do we do with each?
expected: Inventory table with handling from the policy: email tokenize, mobile mask (phone), dob drop, full_name mask
street_address is an address hint the policy does not cover: [TO BE BASELINED — owner: Privacy officer]
Match rate and match count are not estimated: marked to be baselined from the scan, with the scan_pii.py command given
full_name and street_address flagged as name/address hints for human confirmation; states it is not a legal determination

cases.prompt: Our 'contact' column holds a mix of email addresses and phone numbers. Policy: email,mask and phone,tokenize. What handling does that column get?
expected: Handling is tokenize, the strictest of the column's types (drop > tokenize > mask > allow)
Explains the column carries both types and that both are covered by the policy

cases.prompt: Support-ticket export for a summarisation model: ticket_id, subject, body, agent_email, created_at. Policy: email,mask. Inventory it.
expected: agent_email handled mask per the policy
subject and body flagged as free-text columns needing human review regardless of match rate
Any other PII type the free text may carry and the policy omits is [TO BE BASELINED — owner: Privacy officer]; examples, if any, are masked only

cases.prompt: Marketing propensity model extract: member_id, email, zip_code_bucket, tenure_months. Our policy says email,allow. Anything to flag?
expected: email handling is allow per the policy, and the column is listed for a lawful-basis check because it is used in clear
Does not override the policy with its own handling

cases.prompt: Web-log sample for an anomaly model: ts, client_ip (contains both IPv4 and IPv6 addresses), user_agent, user_id. Policy: ipv4,drop. Nothing about IPv6.
expected: client_ip carries ipv4 and ipv6; because ipv6 is missing from the policy the column is [TO BE BASELINED — owner: Privacy officer], not silently drop
Handling gaps section lists ipv6 for the Privacy officer

cases.prompt: VP Data: quick answer — can we send our loyalty extract (member_id, email, card_number, dob) to a vendor's hosted model? Policy: email,tokenize; payment_card,drop.
expected: card_number drop and email tokenize per the policy; dob is not covered: [TO BE BASELINED — owner: Privacy officer]
Recommends running with strict as the gate before data moves to a lower-trust environment: the uncovered dob column would fail the run
States the inventory is sample- and pattern-based and not a legal determination
